Skin grafts and flaps: 4

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

After graft placement, a collection of blood lifts the graft away from the underlying wound surface. Which mechanical complication threatens adherence and nutrient exchange, increasing the risk that the transferred skin will fail?

  1. Skin graft
  2. Tissue flap
  3. A viable vascular recipient bed
  4. Venous congestion of a flap
  5. Blood or fluid separating graft from bed
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Blood or fluid separating graft from bed

A hematoma or seroma can prevent adherence and nutrient exchange, threatening graft take.

Understanding the options

Blood or fluid separating graft from bed
A hematoma or seroma can prevent adherence and nutrient exchange, threatening graft take.
Skin graft
A graft is transferred without its own intact blood supply and initially depends on the recipient bed. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Tissue flap
A flap retains or has surgically restored its own blood supply. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
A viable vascular recipient bed
Graft survival depends on contact with a suitable perfused bed and subsequent revascularization. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Venous congestion of a flap
A dark swollen flap with abnormal refill can indicate impaired venous drainage and needs urgent review. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
